prompt:
Create a high-fidelity desktop web app UI composition for a new Analytics workspace in the existing ASC Studio application. Use the attached ASC Studio Overview screenshot strictly as the identity and chrome reference: preserve its exact left sidebar proportions, top bar height, light neutral canvas, white flat panels, blue accent, Inter-like typography, thin gray hairlines, compact 7–9px corner radii, restrained status colors, readable 13–17px operational text, and shadowless professional operator feel. Do not copy the Overview page's content or panel arrangement.

Viewport is a wide 1919×1088 desktop app screenshot. Keep the existing sidebar and app picker. Insert Analytics directly below Overview in the sidebar and make Analytics the active soft-blue row. Existing items TestFlight, Releases, Apple Ads, Reviews remain visible. Header: "Analytics" with subtitle "Portfolio performance and app-level drivers." Right side has date range "Last 30 days", Compare "Previous period", Filters, and a quiet "Refresh" control. All visualized values are clearly labeled "Sample data" in a small neutral badge so no screenshot implies live facts.

Direction: PORTFOLIO PULSE. This is an adaptive portfolio roster feeding an app-level investigation, not a generic KPI dashboard. Inside the main workspace, create a single master-detail operating surface. On the left, a 360px-wide compact "Apps" roster with five sample apps, each row showing app icon, name, one primary outcome, period delta, and one tiny quiet sparkline. Select "GLP-1 Peptide Tracker" with a soft-blue background and blue edge. Other rows may be "Orbit Notes", "Field Log", "Pocket Pantry", "Trail Conditions". Above the roster are controls "All apps" and "Material changes"; below it a concise note says portfolio ranking uses the selected metric and comparison. No loud cards.

The selected app owns the broad right canvas. Start with a compact four-column metric strip: Downloads 12,480 +8.4%, Conversion 32.7% +1.6 pt, Proceeds $18,420 +11.2%, Active devices 7,920 -2.3%. Each value includes a small source and freshness line; active devices explicitly says "Usage opt-in 24%". Dominant focal moment: a broad dual-period line chart titled "Selected app performance" with Downloads selected in a metric switcher, blue current line and muted previous-period line, release annotation Aug 6, and no decorative fill. Above or beside the chart, include a quiet "Sample data" badge.

Below the chart use one ranked driver table rather than a collage: columns Driver, Current, Previous, Change, Contribution. Rows include United States, Mexico, App Store Search, Product page GLP-1 Basics, and iOS 18.5. Use restrained horizontal contribution bars. On the far right or at the table head, a compact "Inspect" control lets users change breakdown between Territory, Source, Product page, and Version. Add one thin evidence strip across the bottom: "Freshness & coverage" with engagement complete through Aug 17, downloads through Aug 19, privacy-suppressed rows shown as missing, not zero. Include a small contextual action "Open acquisition analysis" rather than a generic CTA.

Preserve context: selecting an app changes the right-hand evidence while the portfolio roster stays visible; this is the signature interaction. No saved-view notebook rail, no question cards, no card-grid portfolio dashboard. Use line charts and semantic HTML-style controls, no gradients, no glass, no oversized typography, no bento-card collage, no fake AI sparkle motif, no dark theme, no 3D, no illustrations. The surface's job must read instantly as compare apps, then explain the selected app's movement. Produce only the UI screenshot, no surrounding device frame, no browser chrome, no caption outside the app.
